## WebSocket connection

Metrics are streamed in real-time via WebSocket:

| Status | Indicator |
|--------|-----------|
| **Connected** | :material-circle:{style="color: #4caf50"} Live updates active |
| **Connecting** | :material-circle:{style="color: #ff9800"} Establishing connection |
| **Disconnected** | :material-circle:{style="color: #f44336"} No live updates |

The frontend automatically reconnects if the connection drops.

---

## Configuration

### Update interval

Open **Metrics → Settings** to adjust collection and history settings. Change the intended value, select the displayed **Apply** action, and check that live values/history continue updating.

Configure how frequently metrics are updated:

| Setting | Default | Range |
|---------|---------|-------|
| Interval | 2 seconds | 0.5-10 seconds |

Lower intervals provide more responsive updates but increase network traffic.

### History settings

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| **Retention** | 7 days | How long to keep history |
| **Bucket Size** | 5 seconds | Aggregation interval |
| **History read backend** | SQLite | Serve history from local SQLite or optional DUMB-managed PostgreSQL |
| **Max local SQLite size** | 100 MB | Bounds the compressed local history/continuity payloads |
| **SQLite continuity path** | `/config/metrics/metrics.sqlite` | Persistent local history database and PostgreSQL write-ahead continuity buffer |

### History storage status

Open **Metrics → Settings → History Storage** to see:

- the configured and currently active provider;
- whether automatic SQLite fallback is active;
- local and PostgreSQL sample counts and allocated size;
- the local compressed-to-original JSON ratio;
- retained legacy JSONL files and import state;
- the latest safe PostgreSQL connection error.

SQLite is the default local history store. PostgreSQL is an optional alternative for history reads; DUMB keeps local history available if PostgreSQL is temporarily unavailable.

<details class="geek-details" markdown="1">
<summary>Technical details: PostgreSQL history and SQLite continuity</summary>

PostgreSQL is not merely a backup. When selected, synchronized, and healthy, it is the active history query and retention backend. SQLite is written first as a bounded write-ahead continuity buffer so live charts remain available when PostgreSQL is stopped or restarting. Retained local samples are replayed when PostgreSQL reconnects.
</details>



On current backends, choosing PostgreSQL only changes the draft selection. The panel explicitly prompts the user to click **Apply & activate PostgreSQL**; nothing is provisioned until that button is used. Apply enables PostgreSQL if necessary, creates the dedicated database, starts or reuses the managed process, synchronizes retained samples, and switches history reads without restarting DUMB. During the operation the panel displays activation progress. Afterward, a persistent **PostgreSQL cutover complete** notice confirms that PostgreSQL is serving history reads while SQLite remains the continuity buffer.

If any step fails, the panel keeps SQLite active and returns to the pending state so **Apply & activate PostgreSQL** can be used to retry. For backward compatibility, dmbdb shows **Apply** plus restart guidance instead when the connected backend does not advertise hot activation support.

Use **Import JSONL now** to force a fresh scan for history created by older DUMB releases. The import is timestamp-idempotent, detects files added after an earlier completed migration, and does not delete the source files. **Refresh / probe** performs an operator-requested PostgreSQL connection test without waiting for the normal retry interval.

See [Metrics history storage](../features/metrics.md#metrics-history-storage) for configuration, sizing, migration, fallback, and rollback details.

---

## Alert thresholds

Configure when alerts appear on the dashboard:

| Resource | Default | Setting Location |
|----------|---------|-----------------|
| CPU | 85% | Metrics header warning controls |
| Memory | 85% | Metrics header warning controls |
| Disk | 90% | Metrics header warning controls |
| Inodes | 90% | Metrics header warning controls |
| Database Health | Off; selectable Moderate/High/Critical minimum | Metrics header or Metrics Settings :material-arrow-right: Database Health Monitoring |

Alerts appear as banners when thresholds are exceeded and on the global Metrics indicator. **DB health** / **Include Database Health in alerts** is optional and browser-local; enabling it does not enable collection for any service or alter its pressure score.

These browser alerts are separate from [backend notifications](../features/notifications.md). Backend notifications continue operating without an open browser and have their own persistent thresholds, cooldowns, recovery handling, and delivery history.

---

<details class="geek-details" markdown="1">
<summary>Technical alternative: query metrics through the API</summary>

## API access

Metrics are also available via the REST API:

```bash
# Current metrics snapshot
curl http://localhost:3005/api/metrics

# Historical metrics newer than a Unix timestamp
curl "http://localhost:3005/api/metrics/history?since=1784300000&limit=5000"

# Storage, migration, and fallback status
curl "http://localhost:3005/api/metrics/history/storage?probe_postgresql=true"

# Database health, optionally forcing a fresh collection
curl "http://localhost:3005/api/metrics/database-health?process_name=InfiniDysk&refresh=true"
```

See the [WebSocket API](../api/websocket.md) documentation for real-time streaming.

---
</details>

## Troubleshooting

### Metrics not updating

- Check WebSocket connection status
- Verify browser supports WebSocket
- Check for network/firewall issues

### High memory usage

- Review per-process metrics to identify heavy services
- Consider disabling unused services
- Increase container memory limits

### Disk filling up

- Check log file sizes
- Review metrics retention settings
- Clear old data if needed

# Onboarding

Onboarding selects services, collects their settings, and starts the chosen stack. It opens on a fresh installation; use **Settings → Onboarding → Launch Onboarding** to run it again.

Existing application data is retained, but the wizard can apply new settings. Use a service's own configuration editor for an ordinary setting change. Onboarding is not a database or namespace migration.

## Before you begin

Have the intended storage mounted inside DUMB, provider credentials ready, and a plan for which application owns requests, downloads, imports, and playback. A host-only mount or browser-reachable URL may not be visible from inside the container.



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

A compatible backend retains a setup checklist after you leave the wizard. It records configured actions, failed checks, missing inputs, and manual work separately. A running process does not complete an arrangement. See [Setup checklist and automation](../features/setup-checklist.md).

</div>



## Wizard steps

### Step 1: Choose services

Select your workflow applications and supporting services, or use **Guided setup**:

1. Choose **Debrid**, **Usenet**, or **Both**.
2. For Usenet, choose Decypharr, InfiniDysk, AltMount, or a supported combination.
3. Decide whether to use Arrs; Usenet arrangements require them.
4. Choose **Combined** or **Separate** Arr instances when using several workflows.
5. Optionally choose separate quality-tier Sonarr/Radarr instances.
6. Select supporting services and choose **Apply recommendations**.

| Layout | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Combined | One Arr instance can use several `core_service` values |
| Separate | Independent Arr instances per workflow |
| Multi-quality | Additional Sonarr/Radarr instances per quality tier |

A tier name such as `1080p` is an instance label, not proof that the application has the intended quality profile.



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

The manual catalog groups services by role, with alphabetical expandable categories and service descriptions. **Expand all** and **Collapse all** change only the layout. Selected categories open initially; summaries retain selection counts when closed.

Review **Chosen by you**, **Required dependency**, and **Optional companion** separately. The historical Core/Optional catalog names do not make every core service mandatory.

</div>



### Step 2: Preflight checks

The wizard checks whether DUMB can continue setup and shows any problems it finds. Read each result, correct blocking errors, then run the check again before continuing.




<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

Health, capability, and catalog failures block the next step. Storage-path inventory and embedded UI checks are advisory. Unknown storage, remote timeout, or consumer-namespace results stay **Not verified** rather than being reported as passed. Correct confirmed critical failures before starting.

</div>



### Step 3: Configure provider credentials

Enter the credentials requested by the selected workflow. Debrid API keys are available from the provider's account page. DUMB maps supported inputs into the selected services' configuration.

An NNTP provider account and an NZB indexer account serve different purposes; supplying one does not configure the other.

### Step 4: Choose companion services

Select optional tools that fit the chosen workflow. Required dependencies can be added automatically and may not appear as separate choices. Already enabled optional services remain visible but cannot be selected as new installations.

Authelia appears only when the backend supports its managed integration. A newer frontend cannot enable an unsupported service on an older API.

| Application | First-start consideration |
| --- | --- |
| mediastorm | Use its [initial credential flow](../services/optional/mediastorm.md#initial-setup) and replace the bootstrap password |
| AIOStreams | Set a stable public HTTPS base URL for remote clients and create its dashboard login |
| Authelia / TPA / Cloudflared | Review public origins, DNS, and authentication routes separately from embedded UI access |

### Step 5: Service-specific options

Review paths, ports, mount mode, media-server settings, and requested provider/database options. Defaults are starting values, not a validation of your deployment.

For Decypharr and AltMount, choose FUSE, embedded rclone, external rclone, or no-mount mode where offered. AltMount still needs an administrator, NNTP provider, import strategy, and valid consumer paths; use its [first-start checklist](../services/core/altmount.md#first-start-checklist).

InfiniDysk 1's `postgres_enabled` and `postgres_database` options are for a fresh installation. They do not copy an existing SQLite library. Existing installations must use the guarded [database migration workflow](../features/arr-postgres-migration.md), after any required namespace migration.



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

For InfiniDysk 2, review the separate runtime and mount choices. Generation 1 retains historical rclone; generation 2 can use rclone-over-WebDAV or native FUSE. FUSE needs a visible device, permissions, and the same mount in every consumer namespace.

Choosing generation 2 opens its guarded installation/migration tool without accepting its acknowledgements or starting a job. Finish the tool, then refresh the setup plan. Existing 1.x data needs major migration; selecting an option does not convert it. Native FUSE omits the associated rclone dependency. See [InfiniDysk 2 installation and upgrade](../features/infinidysk-v2-migration.md).

### Connections and choices

Choose exact application instances, authorized external services, provider-account allocations, library paths, quality profiles, languages, and default/4K request routes. **External server** and **No media server** are separate choices.

Some profiles, roots, and generated keys are available only after first start. Leave those tasks unfinished and return to them later. Existing unowned settings require a reviewed adoption before DUMB changes them.

</div>



### Embedded service access

Enable embedded UIs when offered to use proxied service tabs, split view, and direct links. This does not publish public DNS or configure an external HTTPS origin.

### Review configuration

Review selected services, dependencies, credentials, instance paths, and custom options before applying. Confirmation can install, configure, and start services.



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

The plan groups work into **DUMB will configure**, **Information you must provide**, and **Finish manually**. Choose **Start services** to apply the reviewed plan.

### Setup progress and retained tasks

Follow the checklist and live logs. Correct the relevant input, then apply, retry, or recheck that action. **Continue to dashboard** leaves the wizard without discarding unfinished work; the same checklist appears on the dashboard and matching service pages.

Manual completion records your confirmation separately from an independently passed check. Closing the browser does not complete remaining tasks. External provider/account setup and unsupported connections remain visible as manual work.

</div>




## Skipping onboarding

Use onboarding for the guided setup. If you leave before finishing, open **Settings → Onboarding → Launch Onboarding** to return. Keep track of unfinished provider, account, library, and connection steps; a running service may still need them.

<details class="geek-details" markdown="1">
<summary>Technical alternative: configure services without the wizard</summary>

Set the appropriate `enabled` flags and required paths/credentials through the service configuration or runtime configuration. Disabled applications will not start merely because their files already exist. Do not skip setup steps by guessing a generated API key or database selector.
</details>



<details class="geek-details" markdown="1">
<summary>Technical details: saved configuration and deployment overrides</summary>

## Configuration applied

The wizard updates the runtime `dumb_config.json`, including enabled services, selected provider inputs, service options, and instances. Higher-priority environment or secret values still apply. See [configuration precedence](../features/configuration.md#configuration-precedence).
</details>

## Multi-instance support

Instances need distinct names, process identities, ports, and appropriate data paths. Combined Arr layouts can use list-based `core_service`; separate layouts keep independent integrations. Review the [multi-instance guide](../reference/instances.md) before changing a working topology.



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

## External media and Plex authorization

External endpoints must be reachable from DUMB and require explicit authorization for private-network access. The media-server choice becomes the initial connection choice for selected request/maintenance applications; review each form before applying.

Plex can be claimed from its retained account task after it is ready. Use a fresh short-lived claim token when needed. Existing claimed servers retain their account; claim inputs and API tokens remain masked.

</div>



## After onboarding

Check service status, actual application configuration, and one intended end-to-end workflow. Configure [media-library protection](../features/media-library-protection.md) before unattended storage maintenance, and keep application data backed up.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| A step blocks Next | Read its validation error; check required fields and backend reachability |
| Service fails to start | Inspect its logs, dependencies, configured ports, and mount access |
| Existing service is not offered again | Use its service page; the wizard filters already-enabled selections |
| Need a different topology | Review the change in onboarding; use dedicated migration tools for existing data |



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

Refreshing loses unsaved credential drafts, but the backend's retained setup run remains. Resume its checklist rather than reinstalling successful services.

</div>

# Service pages

Select a service card to open its status, configuration, logs, and application interface. Frequent controls stay in the command bar; less frequent tools are grouped under **Tools**, beside the tab strip. The tools shown depend on the service and connected backend.

## Choose a task

| Task | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Start, stop, or restart | Command bar |
| Change DUMB-managed settings | DUMB Config |
| Edit the application's configuration | Service Config, when available |
| Read or download logs | Service Logs, when available; otherwise sidebar Realtime Logs |
| Open the application's own UI | Embedded UI |
| Check/install an update | Tools → Updates |
| Inspect a missing dependency | Tools → Dependencies |
| Diagnose with selected evidence | AI Assist |
| Change the page's default tab | Tools → Preferences |



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

## Setup checklist

Retained setup tasks are scoped to the current service and instance. Expand **Configure this step** to supply missing inputs, then apply, retry, or recheck the intended action. Manual completion records your confirmation separately from a passed connection test. See [Setup checklist](../features/setup-checklist.md).

</div>



## Status and controls

The header shows process status, application health, and restart information. Hover a health badge for the backend's probe reason. **Starting** and **Degraded** are distinct from a restart-relevant **Unhealthy** result.

Use **Start**, **Stop**, or **Restart** for the current service. The DUMB API page has no start/stop/restart buttons. A storage operation affecting a protected media server prompts for playback and scan handling before it runs. Dashboard bulk updates use safe mode; use the individual service page to review an override.

**Save to File** persists a configuration. Its DUMB Config split-button also offers **Apply in Memory** for a temporary controller change. Saving configuration does not necessarily restart or reconfigure the application.

### InfiniDysk namespace migration

An eligible legacy NzbDAV installation shows its retained migration notice. Choose compatibility-only branding or run the complete namespace preflight. A fresh canonical InfiniDysk installation does not receive this action.

The full cutover requires a current preflight and downtime acknowledgements. It shows a persistent background job with **Open progress**; navigation or browser refresh reattaches to that job. Restarting DUMB interrupts the job rather than resuming it automatically.

| Result | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| Completed | Perform the [post-migration checks](../services/core/infinidysk.md#after-the-full-migration-succeeds), including paths, scans, and sample playback |
| Failed and rolled back | Verify the legacy stack before retrying |
| Interrupted / rollback attention required | Preserve the named backup and follow the reported targeted recovery; do not toggle providers or move paths manually |

**Review cleanup**, where offered after success, is an irreversible purge of migration recovery/history data. Keep independent backups and complete validation before using it. See the [namespace migration procedure](../services/core/infinidysk.md#migration-from-nzbdav) and [cleanup instructions](../services/core/infinidysk.md#finalize-the-migration-and-remove-recovery-data).

### Reset / Remove

**Reset DUMB configuration** disables the target and restores its DUMB defaults. **Remove service files** additionally removes the exact managed paths listed in its preview. The dialog identifies retained/shared paths and requires the exact process name.

Neither operation is a database reset or media-library cleanup. Read [Service reset and removal](../features/service-reset.md), especially for database-backed services and dependencies.

### Rclone Optimizer tab

Eligible InfiniDysk-backed rclone instances show file selection, safety limits, background progress, candidate results, and apply/rollback controls. The production mount supplies discovery metadata; test reads use isolated shadow mounts and can consume provider traffic.

Set limits for your own hardware, connection budget, and provider. A winning profile is a combined result, not proof that each flag is independently optimal. Missing matched provider evidence is shown as unavailable. Apply/rollback interrupts rclone and verifies mount replacement. Use [Rclone Streaming Optimizer](../features/rclone-optimizer.md) before starting a test.

## mediastorm first-login credential

On supported backends, a masked credential notice appears while mediastorm's bootstrap credential file exists. Reveal/copy it only as needed. Current builds require a replacement password during first login; pinned older builds may require changing it immediately after sign-in. The notice disappears when the bootstrap file is removed. See [mediastorm setup](../services/optional/mediastorm.md#initial-setup).

## Database Migration panel

Supported services expose **Database Migration** through backend capability metadata. The panel separates preflight, rehearsal, guarded cutover, and rollback. A successful rehearsal is required before the frontend enables cutover.

Closing the panel does not cancel the backend job. Reopen it to follow progress. InfiniDysk failures, interruption, or rollback problems retain a recovery banner after navigation and reload; use the reported guarded rollback rather than manual provider/file changes.

The [SQLite-to-PostgreSQL guide](../features/arr-postgres-migration.md) lists supported applications, schema checks, backup requirements, and the limits of rollback.



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

For InfiniDysk 2, the frontend selects the separate [native conversion tool](../features/infinidysk-v2-migration.md#native-postgresql-conversion) for the active generation.

</div>



## Dependency graph view

Open **Tools → Dependencies** to inspect startup order, missing prerequisites, and relationship signals. Available **Fix now** actions start the identified dependency; review the target before using them.

| View | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Runtime scope | Hard runtime and explicitly configured dependencies |
| All scope | Runtime edges plus soft/optional application links |
| Details | Dependency reasons and current states |
| Flow | Mermaid graph and parallel prerequisite groups |

Instance links are scoped to the current workflow. An unrelated rclone or Zurg instance is not treated as a valid dependency when the intended mapping is missing. Conditional startup dependencies apply only when the relevant services are enabled. Signals distinguish runtime waits, configured `core_service` links, and optional integrations.

With [Geek Mode](settings.md#geek-mode), the panel also exposes API latency, **Copy JSON**, and raw Mermaid source. Use Details if the browser cannot render Flow.

## Process Metrics panel

Geek Mode adds a Process Metrics panel with PID, uptime, CPU/RSS, I/O, ports, connection count, configured paths, container resources, and restart history. It fetches on page entry; **Refresh** requests a new sample.

### Database Health panel

Supported services expose Database Health independently of Geek Mode. Choose **Standard / passive** or **Enhanced / read-only probes** explicitly for the intended service. Opening the panel does not enable collection.

Expanded results include provider/store information, pressure reasons, database/WAL size, filesystem capacity and inodes, network/read-only state, log signals, and bounded probe results where supported. Plex while running, Decypharr append logs, Phalanx Hyperbee, and Zurg state remain passive-only.

**Ignore network storage score** excludes only intentional network placement; low space, inodes, read-only storage, and other signals still count. The panel does not run maintenance, repairs, integrity checks, or migration. See [Database Health](../features/metrics.md#database-health-monitoring) for interpretation and limits.

## Auto-restart policy

Use **Tools → Auto-restart** to select the current service and set its policy. Global defaults and per-service overrides control the interval, failure threshold, restart window, explicit backoff delays, and grace period.

Monitoring pauses during stack startup. A restart is counted as successful only after the service passes its health check. **Starting** and **Degraded** states remain visible without incrementing the unhealthy threshold. See [Auto-restart](../features/auto-restart.md) before changing limits.

![Auto-restart controls](../assets/images/frontend/auto_restart.png){ .shadow }

## Auto-update settings

| Action | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| Check for updates | Refresh available version/source information without installing |
| Install update | Apply the reported available update |
| Install configured release/branch/commit | Install the saved source target without overriding it |
| Override + latest | Bypass saved source/version selectors for one install |

The automatic schedule has an enable switch, start time in `HH:MM`, interval in hours, and—on supported backends—**Show on dashboard** or **Install automatically**. Saving reschedules the updater; fixed source selections can disable scheduling.

Checks and installs keep progress when you close their panel or navigate within the app. A background banner reopens the active result. DUMB Frontend updates build a candidate while the current frontend remains running, then briefly disconnect during activation. The page reconnects, reads the backend's retained result, and reloads after confirmed success. An unconfirmed reconnect asks you to review stored status.

Where `update_timing_metrics` is supported, **Install** measures the full operation and **Downtime** measures from stopping the old managed process to verified application readiness. The DUMB API's release notice never replaces the Docker container automatically.

[Auto-update](../features/auto-update.md) explains source strategies and protection prompts. [Install cache](../features/install-cache.md#dashboard-maintenance) covers the dashboard's capability-gated cache usage and cleanup tools.

## Seerr Sync panel

On Seerr pages, **Tools → Seerr Sync** configures the primary/subordinate role, polling, external instances, request options, connection tests, and failed-request status. API keys are masked by default. See [Seerr Sync](../features/seerr-sync.md) for the one-way workflow.

## Configuration editors

### Edit DUMB Config

1. Open **DUMB Config** for the selected service or instance.
2. Change the intended fields in the editor. Keep the existing structure and correct any validation errors.
3. Review the added, changed, and removed settings. Acknowledge highlighted sensitive changes only when intended.
4. Select **Save to File** to keep the change after DUMB restarts. **Apply in Memory**, when offered, is temporary.
5. Reopen the tab to confirm the saved value. Follow the service guide for any required restart/setup action, then check its health and logs.

Invalid JSON or validation errors block saves. Command, path, credential, and networking changes can require acknowledgement.

On the DUMB API page, **DUMB API Logging** can temporarily enable DEBUG without a restart when supported. It shows configured/effective levels and clears the override on container restart. It does not change application log levels. If DEBUG is configured persistently, edit the saved configuration to disable it.

### Edit Service Config

1. Open **Service Config** when the application provides this tab.
2. Change the intended application setting and select **Save Service Config**.
3. Reopen the editor to confirm the saved value. Follow the application's restart/setup instructions and verify the result in its own interface.

Application settings and DUMB-managed settings are separate. Use the [service guide](../services/index.md) to find the correct editor and restart requirements.

![Edit Service Config](../assets/images/frontend/edit_service_config.png){ .shadow }

## AI Assist

1. Choose a diagnostic preset and time/comparison window.
2. Select **Preview bundle** to inspect redacted evidence without a provider call.
3. Select **Analyze** when ready to send that evidence.
4. Review coverage and confidence before acting on the response.

Saved provider profiles are shared with Stack AI Assist. Keys stay server-side. Editing a profile's details marks it unsaved; selecting a different provider does not silently overwrite the saved profile. Deep scans inspect retained backend logs within the configured MiB budget, rather than only the visible log rows.

The [AI Assistant guide](../features/ai-assistant.md) covers supported models, provider setup, redaction, and evidence limitations.

## Logs

Filter by text or level, choose a line limit, follow the tail, refresh, or download a snapshot. Service-aware parsing retains application timestamps/severity and groups multiline errors where supported. Traefik offers access logs; Plex offers DBRepair logs when enabled.

DUMB applies its sensitive-data redactor to logs viewed or downloaded here. Review a download before sharing it; arbitrary application output can contain values the redactor does not recognize.

![View service logs](../assets/images/frontend/view_service_logs.png){ .shadow }

## Embedded UI

Enable service UIs in Settings, then open the service's **Embedded UI** tab. Choose its supported base path, use split/full-window view, or open the direct link. A matching enabled TPA HTTPS route can supply a public link; otherwise use the local/private link.

DUMB login does not replace the application's own login. Root-relative APIs, assets, and WebSockets use the frontend's service context. Authelia login and TPA admin SSO open at their public HTTPS origins in a top-level tab.



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

InfiniDysk 2 currently opens at its own root URL. Use the direct local/public address until a validated embedded adapter is advertised; do not substitute a subpath URL into signed playback links.

</div>



### Service workers and browser notifications

Embedded workers are scoped to the owning service to preserve background updates and destination routing. This routing does not isolate the applications' cookies, CacheStorage, or other storage on the shared frontend origin. Native OS notification delivery also depends on browser and system permissions. A dedicated application origin keeps its own native worker behavior.

### Jellyfin and Emby libraries

Sign in within Embedded UI using an application account allowed to access the libraries. A login at the direct server address may not carry over to the frontend origin. If the same account sees libraries directly but not embedded, update the frontend and reopen the tab; older proxies could incorrectly route library requests under the web client's asset path.

See [Embedded service UIs](../features/embedded-ui.md) for routing and troubleshooting.

## Default tab selection

Use **Tools → Preferences** to choose the default tab, or make the current tab the default. On narrow screens, swipe the tab bar horizontally; edge chevrons indicate hidden tabs.

## Sidebar operator QoL

Use quick status filters, service/config-key search, saved views, compact mode, or `Ctrl/Cmd + K` to find a service. The command palette also supports capturing an assigned service shortcut. **Auto-hide on navigation** is enabled by default and can be disabled for a persistent desktop sidebar.

Sidebar preferences are saved under `dumb.ui.sidebar`. Dashboard drag-and-drop writes `service_order`, which both the dashboard and sidebar use.

Open **Settings** from the sidebar. Expand a section to change its values. Closing a section changes only the layout; it does not disable the feature.

## Appearance

Choose **System Default** to follow your operating system, or select a light/dark palette. This preference is stored in the browser and does not change backend configuration.

## About section

### Version information

The About section shows the installed API, frontend, and service versions. Select an **Update available** badge to open the **DUMB Updates** dialog. Where GitHub history includes the installed release, it also shows how many releases the component is behind. Moving development builds show **Dev build** instead of an invented release count.

Dismissing a banner hides it only in that browser. The About section retains the backend's update result and can show the banner again.



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

Ordinary stable notices are suppressed when the installed version is equal to or newer than that release. Explicit branch, commit, and release selections remain available for review.

</div>



![About settings](../assets/images/frontend/about_settings.png){ .shadow }

### Launch Onboarding

Choose **Launch Onboarding** and confirm to review services again. If onboarding has already completed, you can go directly to optional services.

Existing application data is retained, but the wizard can apply new settings over the current configuration. Already enabled non-instance services are not offered as new selections; use their service pages for ordinary configuration changes.

## Embedded service UIs

Enable **Service UIs** to add embedded application tabs, direct links, and full-window controls to supported service pages. Disabling it removes dashboard access through those routes; native-port access still depends on your deployment's port mappings.

![Embedded UI settings](../assets/images/frontend/embedded_ui_settings.png){ .shadow }

See [Embedded service UIs](../features/embedded-ui.md) for routing, application logins, and Authelia/TPA SSO exceptions.

## Notifications

This section requires the backend's `notifications` capability. It configures outbound delivery that continues without an open browser.

1. Enable notifications and add an Apprise or generic webhook destination.
2. Choose minimum severity, event types, and intended enabled services.
3. Save and test the destination.
4. Review delivery history if a normal event does not arrive.

The default **Warning** minimum excludes normal **Success** events, including successful auto-restarts. **Save & test** bypasses enable switches and routing filters for that test; it does not prove a normal event matches your rules.

Saved destination URLs and headers stay on the server. A blank secret field preserves its existing value. Apprise normally delivers directly from DUMB to the provider; `apprise://` and `apprises://` explicitly use an Apprise API server.

[Notifications](../features/notifications.md) documents events, startup baselining, retries, thresholds, and delivery limitations. Browser-local Metrics banners use separate settings on the Metrics page.

## Token settings

| Token | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| Plex | Plex API access and selected integrations, such as Riven watchlists/scans |
| GitHub | Higher API limits and authorized private/sponsored release downloads |

A GitHub token should grant only the read access required by the selected source. Public release checks normally need no token. Enter the required token here, select **Save**, and wait for **Saved**. Retry the connection or update check that needed it. Technical deployments can also use a supported [configuration override](../features/configuration.md#configuration-precedence).

![Token settings](../assets/images/frontend/tokens_settings.png){ .shadow }

## UI preferences

**Log Timestamp Format** controls MDY/DMY date order, 12/24-hour time, and leading zeros. It changes log presentation, not the backend's timezone or original log timestamps.

![Log timestamp settings](../assets/images/frontend/log_timestamp_settings.png){ .shadow }

## Advanced



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

### Service utilities

Choose **Service or instance**, then a tool for that exact target. The selector includes enabled/running services and instances with saved utility state, and omits unconfigured disabled templates.

Available shortcuts include Media Protection, Symlinks, Database Health/Migration, InfiniDysk 2 migration, Rclone Optimizer, Seerr Sync, and Plex Status. They depend on backend and service capabilities. Opening a tool does not run it or accept its confirmations. Viewing Database Health does not enable collection.

</div>



### Geek Mode

This is a preference in the **DUMB dashboard**, separate from the Geek mode switch in this documentation site's header. The dashboard preference adds diagnostic controls to the application; the docs switch reveals explanations and alternative methods in these guides.

Open **Settings → Advanced → Geek Mode** and enable it for extra diagnostic details. Return to a service page to see the additional controls:

| Location | Additional information |
| --- | --- |
| Service header | Internal config key and process name |
| Dependencies | API latency, Copy JSON, and Mermaid source in Flow |
| Process Metrics | PID, uptime, CPU/RSS, I/O, listening ports, paths, and restart history |
| Dashboard cards | CPU/RSS badges, refreshed every five seconds |
| Supported database services | Summary of explicitly enabled Database Health collection |

Database Health stays opt-in per service. Geek Mode does not run repair, integrity checks, or migrations.

![Auto-restart controls](../assets/images/frontend/auto_restart.png){ .shadow }

## Authentication settings

### Authentication provider

Choose **Local**, **Hybrid**, or **OIDC only** when supported by the connected API. Hybrid retains local login for recovery. OIDC-only requires an explicit lockout-risk confirmation.

The provider editor supports managed/external Authelia and provider presets including Google, Authentik, Keycloak, Entra ID, Auth0, Okta, ZITADEL, Dex, and generic OIDC. Each external provider needs a web application, client ID/secret, and the exact browser-facing HTTPS callback:

```text
https://dumb.example.com/api/auth/oidc/callback
```

Opening Settings through localhost or an IP address leaves the callback blank. Enter the real HTTPS FQDN and register the exact value at the provider. Select **Check discovery**, correct any reported error, then select **Save provider**. Keep Hybrid mode while testing provider sign-in in a separate private browser window.

For bootstrapped DUMB-managed Authelia, **Link managed Authelia** creates/reuses a dedicated client and transfers its secret without displaying it. Use the [Authelia wizard](../services/optional/authelia.md) for bootstrap and route setup.

Provider TLS verification stays enabled by default. **Allow private endpoint IPs** and **Allow HTTP** are explicit outbound connection exceptions for a trusted provider; changing presets resets them. The full [authentication guide](../features/authentication.md#configure-an-oidc-provider) covers claim mapping and provider restrictions.

### Enable/disable authentication

Enable authentication before allowing untrusted network access. Disabling it exposes DUMB controls to anyone who can reach the API.

### User management

Add, disable, enable, or delete local users under Authentication. DUMB protects the last active user from disable/delete. All enabled users have the same operator privileges; groups do not create viewer or administrator roles.

![Authentication settings](../assets/images/frontend/auth_settings.png){ .shadow }



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

## Backups and restore

1. Register an already-mounted destination.
2. Choose `.tar` or `.tar.zst`, then run **Preview backup**.
3. Review coverage, capacity, exclusions, and downtime before confirming archive creation.
4. Follow the application-wide progress notice until completion.

The preview scans while applications remain running. **Cancel preview** waits for its cleanup; closing the page does not cancel backend work. Manual compression and schedule compression are separate choices, and compression does not encrypt an archive.

A fresh installation can reach restore before application onboarding after normal authentication setup/login. **Recovery required** retains instructions and may block service/setup actions until recovery completes. Reconnect after a lost connection to establish the actual terminal state. Do not stop DUMB or the host during a running backup or restore.

Use [Installation backup and restore](../features/installation-backups.md) for the complete procedure and [Backup storage](../features/backup-storage.md) for destination identity and mount checks.

</div>

# Start here

DUMB (Distributed Unlimited Media Bridge) runs your chosen media services in one container and gives you a dashboard to configure, monitor, and update them. You can use Debrid, Usenet, or both, with a media server inside DUMB or on another machine.

You choose the services. You do not need to enable the whole catalog.

Use the documentation channel that matches your image: **Latest release** for stable images or **Development** for `dev`. [How documentation versions work](../reference/doc-versions.md).

## Choose your deployment guide

Start with the guide for your host or management tool:

- [Docker Compose](../deployment/docker.md) · [Portainer](../deployment/portainer.md) · [Dockge](../deployment/dockge.md)
- [Unraid](../deployment/unraid.md) · [Synology](../deployment/synology.md) · [QNAP](../deployment/qnap.md) · [TrueNAS SCALE](../deployment/truenas.md)
- [Windows / WSL2](../deployment/wsl.md) · [Proxmox LXC](../deployment/proxmox.md)

[Compare deployment options](../deployment/index.md). After deployment, continue below with the dashboard and your chosen workflow.

## Choose a workflow

| What you want | Start with |
|---|---|
| Manage a library with Sonarr or Radarr using Debrid | [Decypharr](../services/core/decypharr.md) |
| Manage a Usenet library with Arr applications | [InfiniDysk](../services/core/infinidysk.md) or [AltMount](../services/core/altmount.md); Decypharr also supports native Usenet |
| Use lists, watchlists, or requests with a Debrid workflow | [Riven](../services/core/riven-backend.md) or [CLI Debrid](../services/core/cli-debrid.md) |
| Run a media server | [Plex](../services/core/plex-media-server.md), [Jellyfin](../services/core/jellyfin.md), or [Emby](../services/core/emby.md) |
| Aggregate sources for Stremio | [AIOStreams](../services/optional/aiostreams.md) |
| Add tools to an existing stack | Browse the [service catalog](../services/index.md); onboarding can skip core workflow selection |

These are starting points, not interchangeable backends. Each service has its own provider support, accounts, and library behavior. Check its guide before choosing.

## From install to first playback

<figure class="docs-visual" markdown="1">

![Five stages: prepare, install DUMB, choose services, connect the apps, then import and play a test item.](../assets/images/guides/first-playback.svg)

<figcaption class="docs-visual-caption">Start with one workflow and test a real item from import to playback. The steps below link to the instructions for each stage.</figcaption>
</figure>

1. **Prepare storage and credentials.** Read [Before you install](installation.md).
2. **Deploy DUMB.** Choose your host in [Deployment](../deployment/index.md).
3. **Open the dashboard.** The default address is `http://<host>:3005`.
4. **Complete onboarding.** Select services and enter provider credentials. See [Onboarding](../frontend/onboarding.md).

5. <span class="docs-channel-badge" data-channel="dev" title="Added after the released DUMB 2.23.0 documentation snapshot">Dev</span> **Finish application setup.** Review the [setup checklist](../features/setup-checklist.md), including accounts, indexers, root folders, libraries, and any manual tasks.


6. **Check the workflow.** Add a test item through your chosen application, confirm its import, and play it from the media server. A running process alone does not establish this.

## What runs where

<details class="geek-details" markdown="1">
<summary>Technical details: control and media paths</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    USER([You]) --> FE[Dashboard :3005]
    FE --> API[DUMB controller]
    API --> ARR[Arr applications]
    API --> FLOW[Debrid or Usenet service]
    ARR --> FLOW
    FLOW --> LIB[(Mounts and library paths)]
    LIB --> MEDIA[Plex / Jellyfin / Emby]
    FE -. embedded UI .-> ARR
    FE -. embedded UI .-> FLOW
```

</details>

DUMB installs and coordinates services. Each upstream application still owns its accounts, provider behavior, database, and content decisions. The [architecture guide](../architecture/index.md) explains the boundaries.

!!! tip "Using a media server outside DUMB?"

    Plan the shared paths before installation. An external application must see the library **and the targets of its symlinks**. FUSE submounts may also require Linux mount propagation. See [rclone and external consumers](../services/dependent/rclone.md).

# Before you install

Have a host, persistent storage, and credentials for the services you plan to use. DUMB creates its initial configuration at startup; you do not need to write a complete `dumb_config.json` first.

## Choose your platform first

These guides explain the installation steps for each platform. Use this page to prepare, then follow your selected guide.

- [Docker Compose](../deployment/docker.md) · [Portainer](../deployment/portainer.md) · [Dockge](../deployment/dockge.md)
- [Unraid](../deployment/unraid.md) · [Synology](../deployment/synology.md) · [QNAP](../deployment/qnap.md) · [TrueNAS SCALE](../deployment/truenas.md)
- [Windows / WSL2](../deployment/wsl.md) · [Proxmox LXC](../deployment/proxmox.md)

[Compare deployment options](../deployment/index.md).

## Host requirements

| Requirement | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Docker Engine on Linux, including WSL2; or the [native Proxmox LXC helper](../deployment/proxmox.md) |
| CPU and memory | Start around 2 vCPU and 2 GB RAM for a small stack. This is a planning estimate; source builds, databases, transcoding, and larger service selections need more. |
| Storage | Persistent storage for configuration, databases, logs, and library paths; SSD storage is preferable for databases and source builds. |
| User and group | Non-root `PUID` and `PGID` with access to the host directories. Check them with `id -u` and `id -g`. |
| Networking | Access to image/package registries and your providers. Publish dashboard port `3005` unless you deliberately change it. |

!!! warning "Docker Desktop and external mounts"

    Docker Desktop does not support the bind mount propagation needed to share DUMB-created FUSE/rclone submounts with containers outside DUMB. For Windows, use [Docker Engine inside WSL2](../deployment/wsl.md). See [Docker's propagation documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/bind-mounts/#configure-bind-propagation).

## Accounts and credentials

| Selected integration | Have this ready |
|---|---|
| Debrid | API key for each selected provider |
| Usenet | NNTP host, port, username/password, connection limit, and TLS setting |
| Plex | Claim/token and server address when the selected integration requires them |
| Private or sponsored GitHub repository | A read-capable GitHub token with the access that repository requires |
| Cloudflared | A Cloudflare Tunnel token |

You only need credentials for the integrations you enable. See [integration tokens](../features/configuration.md#integration-tokens-credentials).

## Persistent directories

The maintained Compose layout mounts four host directories. Native LXC uses the same absolute paths directly in the guest.

| Path inside DUMB | Contents |
|---|---|
| `/config` | DUMB configuration, authentication data, migration jobs, snapshots, and feature state |
| `/log` | DUMB and collected service logs |
| `/data` | Persistent application data. DUMB maps internal paths such as `/plex`, `/postgres_data`, and `/decypharr` into subdirectories here. |
| `/mnt/debrid` | Mounts, generated links, and library paths |

Keep these paths when recreating or upgrading the container. Store a separate backup of important configuration and application data; a bind mount alone is not a backup.

!!! note "Existing installations"

    Separate direct mounts such as `/postgres_data` or `/plex` are legacy or advanced layouts. They can prevent DUMB from creating managed data symlinks. Preserve an existing layout until you have reviewed its migration; do not add those mounts to a new deployment by default.

## Decide who reads the library

- **Everything inside DUMB:** use a normal `/mnt/debrid` bind mount.
- **External Arr or media-server containers:** use matching library and target paths. If they need DUMB-created FUSE/rclone submounts, prepare a shared host mount and use `:rshared` on DUMB's bind, with the appropriate consumer propagation.
- **Remote machines:** plan an explicit sharing method. A path that exists inside DUMB does not automatically become available elsewhere.

The need for propagation comes from the deployment topology, not the workflow's name. Adding `:rshared` to Compose does not prepare the host mount.

## Ready to deploy

Choose your [deployment guide](../deployment/index.md), start DUMB, and open `http://<host>:3005`. Then follow [onboarding](../frontend/onboarding.md).

Review the retained [setup checklist](../features/setup-checklist.md) for automatic and manual integration tasks.

</div>

# Configuration schema

DUMB uses a JSON schema to validate `/config/dumb_config.json` and keep service definitions consistent.

## Schema location

The default template and schema live in the backend repository/image:

```
utils/dumb_config.json
utils/dumb_config_schema.json
```

`utils/dumb_config.json` is a template; `/config/dumb_config.json` is the persistent runtime file. On startup DUMB copies the template when needed, adds missing defaults to existing configs, prunes keys removed from the supported template, and validates the result against the schema before creating the effective environment-overridden configuration.

The API exposes the current schema at native `GET /config/schema` (frontend proxy: `GET /api/config/schema`) and a process-specific subtree at `POST /config/process-config/schema`.

## Top-level structure

| Key | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| `puid` / `pgid` | Container user/group IDs |
| `tz` | Time zone string |
| `data_root` | Base path for persisted data |
| `dumb` | DUMB core settings (API, frontend, logging, tokens) |
| `traefik` | Reverse-proxy configuration |
| `traefik_proxy_admin` / `cloudflared` | Optional reverse-proxy management and tunnel connector |
| `seerr_sync` | Cross-instance Seerr synchronization |
| `postgres` / `pgadmin` | Database settings |
| `rclone` | rclone instances and mounts |
| Service keys | Core/dependent/optional services (for example `decypharr`, `infinidysk`, `aiostreams`, `cli_debrid`) |

!!! note "Service blocks are explicit"

    Each service has its own schema definition (for example `decypharr`, `infinidysk`, `cli_debrid`). This ensures consistent required fields and defaults.

## Validation tips

- Validate JSON changes before restart to avoid startup failures.
- Back up `/config/dumb_config.json` before large manual edits; use the frontend editor for normal service changes.
- Keep `config_dir`, `log_file`, and `port` unique for each service instance.
- Use `release_version_enabled` for release tags, `commit_sha` for an exact
  40-character GitHub source revision, or `branch_enabled` for a moving branch.
- A non-empty `commit_sha` takes precedence over release and branch settings and
  disables automatic updates until changed or cleared.
- Do not edit `utils/dumb_config.json` expecting a persistent runtime change.

## Related pages

- [Environment variables](environment-variables.md)
- [Multi-instance configuration](instances.md)

# Core service routing

`core_service` is the flag DUMB uses to route automation between Arrs and the core
download workflows. It keeps Debrid- and Usenet-based stacks isolated while
still allowing multiple instances of the same Arr service.

## Where `core_service` is used

| Config block | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| Arr instances (`sonarr`, `radarr`, `lidarr`, `whisparr`) | Selects the download workflow(s) to auto-wire. |
| NeutArr instances | Filters which Arr instances are sent to NeutArr. |
| Profilarr instances | Filters which Arr instances are auto-linked to Profilarr. |
| rclone/zurg instances | Labels the instance for the workflow it supports. |

## Routing map

```mermaid
%%{ init: { "flowchart": { "curve": "basis" } } }%%
flowchart TD
    ARR[Arr instances]
    CS{core_service}
    DEC[Decypharr Debrid/Usenet workflow]
    NZB[InfiniDysk workflow]
    ALT[AltMount workflow]
    PROWLARR[Prowlarr apps + tags]
    IDX[Tagged indexers]
    NEUTARR[NeutArr instance]
    PROFILARR[Profilarr instance]

    ARR ==> CS
    CS -- decypharr --> DEC
    CS -- infinidysk --> NZB
    CS -- altmount --> ALT
    DEC ==> PROWLARR
    NZB ==> PROWLARR
    ALT ==> PROWLARR
    PROWLARR ==> IDX
    IDX ==> ARR
    CS ==> NEUTARR
    CS ==> PROFILARR
```

## Supported values

Use one or more of the core workflow keys:

| Value | Workflow | Typical use |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `decypharr` | Debrid and/or Usenet workflow | Decypharr torrent and Sabnzbd-compatible Arr clients |
| `infinidysk` | Usenet workflow | InfiniDysk + Usenet indexers |
| `altmount` | Usenet workflow | AltMount SABnzbd-compatible client + Usenet indexers |

Leave `core_service` empty if you do not want DUMB to auto-wire a service into a
workflow. To combine workflows, set `core_service` to a list or use a
comma-separated string.

## What DUMB does with it

When `core_service` is set on an Arr instance, DUMB:

- Configures matching download clients (Decypharr, InfiniDysk, and/or AltMount).
- Adds or updates Arr root folders and permissions where that workflow's setup
  hook owns them. AltMount configures the download-client connection but leaves
  its import strategy and Arr root folders operator-managed.
- Creates Prowlarr apps tagged with the same core service(s) so indexers sync
  only to the intended Arrs.

When `core_service` combines Decypharr with InfiniDysk or AltMount, DUMB uses the
shared `/mnt/debrid/combined_symlinks/<slug>` base for the Decypharr-owned Arr
root. InfiniDysk without Decypharr keeps its InfiniDysk symlink root, and AltMount does
not independently rewrite the Arr root folder.

When `core_service` is set on a NeutArr instance, DUMB:

- Sends Arr instances whose core services overlap the NeutArr instance.

When `core_service` is set on a Profilarr instance, DUMB:

- Auto-links only Arr instances whose core services overlap the Profilarr instance.
- Seeds profile/custom format/regex/media-management sync for those Arr instances (when `use_profilarr` is enabled on the Arr).

## Example: split Debrid and Usenet workflows

```json
"radarr": {
  "instances": {
    "Debrid": {
      "enabled": true,
      "core_service": "decypharr",
      "use_neutarr": true,
      "use_profilarr": true,
      "port": 7878
    },
    "Usenet": {
      "enabled": true,
      "core_service": "infinidysk",
      "use_neutarr": false,
      "use_profilarr": false,
      "port": 7879
    }
  }
}
```

In this layout:

- The Debrid Radarr instance syncs with Decypharr and Debrid indexers.
- The Usenet Radarr instance links to InfiniDysk because its `core_service` is `infinidysk`. Change that field to select another workflow.
- NeutArr only receives the Debrid instance because `use_neutarr` is set there.
- Profilarr only links the Debrid instance because `use_profilarr` is set there.

## Example: combine workflows on one Arr instance

```json
"sonarr": {
  "instances": {
    "Combined": {
      "core_service": ["decypharr", "infinidysk", "altmount"],
      "use_neutarr": true,
      "use_profilarr": true
    }
  }
}
```

In this layout, DUMB wires Decypharr, InfiniDysk, and AltMount download clients for
the same Sonarr instance. Decypharr and InfiniDysk coordinate the DUMB-managed
combined root; AltMount's import strategy and compatible Arr paths still need
to be reviewed in AltMount.

## Related references

- [Multi-instance setup](instances.md)
- [Prowlarr](../services/core/prowlarr.md)
- [NeutArr](../services/core/neutarr.md)

# Choose the right documentation

The selector in the site header switches between **Latest release** and
**Development**. It shows the DUMB version each channel covers. These numbers
refer to DUMB itself, rather than the documentation site's own releases.

The footer shows **Documentation release** with a separate version number and
a link to its release notes. That number identifies the published guides you
are reading; it is shared by both channels. Include it when reporting a docs
problem. A local or pull-request preview is labelled **unreleased** instead.

| Choose | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| **Latest release** | You run a stable DUMB image, such as `iampuid0/dumb:latest` or a numbered stable tag. |
| **Development** | You run `iampuid0/dumb:dev`, or you want to read about work awaiting a stable release. |

Switching keeps you on the same guide where it exists. A feature that has not
shipped shows an availability page in the release channel with a link to its
development guide. If there is no matching page, the selector opens the other
channel's homepage.

Check the DUMB version shown in the dashboard's **Settings → About** if the
instructions do not match your installation. The dashboard updates independently:
an older dashboard may not show controls supported by its backend, while a newer
one cannot add a missing backend feature to an older DUMB image. Check both
versions in **About**. Individually pinned service versions may also differ from
the examples.

## Use Geek mode when you want more detail

The main guide is for people using the DUMB frontend. It explains where to go,
what to click or enter, how to save the change, and how to check the result.
You should be able to complete that frontend task with Geek mode off.

**Geek mode** adds two kinds of optional material:

| If you want to… | Geek sections provide |
| --- | --- |
| Understand how the feature works | Internal processes, dependencies, request/data flow, and detailed workflow diagrams |
| Use another method | API calls, command-line tools, environment variables, and manual configuration procedures |

For example, the ordinary update guide explains the dashboard's **Check for
updates**, install, and scheduling controls. Its Geek sections explain version
selection and the installer lifecycle, with alternative configuration methods.

The header shows **On** or **Off**. Enabled Geek sections have a light green
background and **Geek detail** label. Your browser remembers the choice, and you
can also open a single section without enabling the whole mode.

Warnings, required frontend steps, deployment guides, community links, and
maintainer support remain visible in both modes. A long frontend procedure is
still a user procedure; it does not become Geek content because it has many steps.

Some pages have no optional Geek sections. Direct links to a heading inside a
closed section open that section so the linked explanation stays reachable.
The [Geek reference](index.md) also provides API, configuration, and architecture
references directly.

This switch changes the documentation display. It does not change DUMB or its
frontend settings. If you see **Geek Mode** inside the DUMB dashboard, that is a
separate setting; see [dashboard Settings](../frontend/settings.md).

## Spot development additions

Each page identifies its documentation channel and DUMB version. **Released
docs** use a blue-green label; **Development docs** use amber. Words accompany
the colors so you can tell them apart without relying on color alone.

In development guides, amber panels and small **Dev** badges identify additions
beyond the released documentation snapshot. A development-only feature page
also states which stable DUMB release does not include that feature. A newly
written guide for an existing feature is labelled **New guide** instead.

## How release docs stay current

The release channel is a snapshot of reviewed documentation. Later development
edits do not silently change its description of the stable image.

A scheduled watcher checks DUMB releases every six hours. When a new stable
release matches the reviewed development version and includes the backend
source covered by that review, the watcher also checks that the compatible
dashboard code has a published stable release. The docs workflow validates and
records that snapshot, then Release Please prepares a documentation release.
After its checks pass, the generated version update merges automatically and
the site publishes from that release's exact source. A maintainer can run the
release check or retry publication manually.

If the release version or source does not match the reviewed documentation,
promotion stops for a maintainer review. This prevents development features
from being presented as released. Shared theme and accessibility fixes can
still apply to both channels.

## Documentation for AI agents

Each channel provides an [`llms.txt`](../llms.txt) index and
[`llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt) with its complete documentation text.
Use the files from the channel matching the installed backend. Technical
details are included regardless of the browser's Geek mode preference.

# Environment variables

DUMB reads startup overrides for supported configuration leaf values from environment variables or Docker secrets. Override names follow the existing configuration tree; they do not create new service instances or arbitrary keys. Service subprocess variables are separately defined under each service's `env` block.

## Container variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `PUID` | `1000` | Managed-service user ID; must be greater than `0` |
| `PGID` | `1000` | Managed-service group ID; must be greater than `0` |
| `TZ` | unset | Time zone (for example `America/New_York`) |
| `DUMB_PNPM_STORE_ROOT` | `/config/.pnpm-store` | Persistent pnpm package store root used during service setup/builds. Override only if `/config` is not suitable. |
| `DUMB_BUN_CACHE_ROOT` | `/config/.bun-cache` | Persistent Bun package cache root used during Bun-based service setup/builds, such as Pulsarr. Override only if `/config` is not suitable. |
| `DUMB_YARN_CACHE_ROOT` | `/config/.yarn-cache` | Persistent Yarn package cache root used during source builds, such as Maintainerr. Override when `/config` is on slower network storage. |

!!! warning "Root IDs are rejected"

    DUMB's controller starts with the container privileges needed to prepare users, ownership, devices, and mounts, then launches managed services with `PUID` and `PGID`. DUMB refuses to start when either value is `0`; choose a non-root host user and group that can access the mounted paths.

!!! tip "Complete generated reference"

    The repository's [`.env.example`](https://github.com/I-am-PUID-0/DUMB/blob/dev/.env.example) is generated from the current config template and contains the complete default set. The table above calls out bootstrap/cache variables operators commonly set directly.

## Config override naming

DUMB joins a configuration path with underscores and uppercases it:

| Config path | Override name |
|---|---|
| `puid` | `PUID` |
| `dumb.github_token` | `DUMB_GITHUB_TOKEN` |
| `dumb.api_service.host` | `DUMB_API_SERVICE_HOST` |
| `altmount.port` | `ALTMOUNT_PORT` |
| `infinidysk.frontend_port` | `INFINIDYSK_FRONTEND_PORT` |
| `sonarr.instances.Default.port` | `SONARR_INSTANCES_DEFAULT_PORT` |

List values use valid JSON, such as `DUMB_METRICS_FILESYSTEM_PATHS=["/","/mnt/debrid"]`. Set dictionary members through their individual leaf names; edit JSON configuration or use the API for structural changes.

## Sources and precedence

For a config override named `DUMB_API_SERVICE_HOST`, DUMB checks:

1. `/run/secrets/DUMB_API_SERVICE_HOST`
2. The process/container environment
3. `/config/.env`
4. The value in `/config/dumb_config.json`

Blank environment values do not replace configured values. Docker secrets are read as trimmed text and have the highest priority.

!!! note "InfiniDysk upgrade compatibility"

    Fresh configurations use the `INFINIDYSK_*` prefix. Existing deployments
    may continue supplying legacy `NZBDAV_*` overrides or Docker secrets;
    DUMB checks those names as fallbacks until the deployment opts into the
    canonical persisted identity.

## Service environment variables

Each service can define variables passed to that subprocess under its `env` block in `/config/dumb_config.json`. These are service runtime variables, not names for overriding DUMB's own config tree.

Example:

```json
"infinidysk": {
  "env": {
    "WEBDAV_USER": "admin",
    "WEBDAV_PASSWORD": "change-me"
  }
}
```

!!! warning "Secrets in config files"

    Treat tokens and passwords in `dumb_config.json` as secrets. Avoid committing them to source control.

- [Config schema](config-schema.md)

# Multi-instance configuration

Several DUMB services support multiple instances (for example Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Whisparr, and rclone). This guide shows how to configure instances safely.

## Instance pattern

Services that support instances use an `instances` map keyed by a friendly name:

```json
"sonarr": {
  "instances": {
    "Default": {
      "enabled": true,
      "process_name": "Sonarr Default",
      "port": 8989,
      "config_dir": "/sonarr/default",
      "config_file": "/sonarr/default/config.xml",
      "log_file": "/sonarr/default/logs/sonarr.txt"
    },
    "Anime": {
      "enabled": true,
      "process_name": "Sonarr Anime",
      "port": 8991,
      "config_dir": "/sonarr/anime",
      "config_file": "/sonarr/anime/config.xml",
      "log_file": "/sonarr/anime/logs/sonarr.txt"
    }
  }
}
```

## Best practices

- Assign unique ports per instance to avoid collisions.
- Use distinct `config_dir` and `log_file` paths.
- Keep `process_name` descriptive for clarity in the UI.
- Set `core_service` when integrating with Decypharr, InfiniDysk, or AltMount (single value, list, or comma-separated).

## rclone instances

rclone also uses an `instances` map for different mount targets:

```json
"rclone": {
  "instances": {
    "Decypharr": {
      "enabled": true,
      "core_service": "decypharr",
      "mount_dir": "/mnt/debrid",
      "mount_name": "decypharr",
      "config_dir": "/config",
      "config_file": "/config/rclone.conf"
    }
  }
}
```

- [Configuration guide](../features/configuration.md)

# Service ports

These are **fresh-configuration defaults**, not a report of your running stack. Check the port saved in the dashboard or `/config/dumb_config.json` before adding a Docker mapping or configuring another application.

The maintained Compose file publishes **3005 only**. It serves the dashboard, REST gateway (`/api/*`), and WebSockets (`/ws/*`). Embedded UIs use this address too; individual service ports are needed for direct clients and external integrations.

## DUMB listeners

| Service | Default port | Access |
|---|---:|---|
| DUMB Frontend and API gateway | 3005 | `http://<host>:3005`; normal entry point |
| DUMB API | 8000 | Container loopback `127.0.0.1`; not published by default |
| Traefik embedded UI proxy | 18080 | Internal frontend proxy target; direct access requires a mapping |
| Traefik dashboard/API | 18081 | Entry point plus one; normally consumed internally |

Use `http://<host>:3005/api/process/processes` for REST requests. WebSocket requests use `ws://<host>:3005/ws/status` without `/api`. See the [API guide](../api/index.md).

## Workflow and media services

| Service | Default port | Purpose / direct path |
|---|---:|---|
| Riven Frontend | 3000 | Web UI |
| Riven Backend | 8080 | API |
| CLI Debrid | 5000 | Web UI |
| CLI Battery | 5001 | API; separate listener only for versions using the external service |
| Decypharr | 8282 | Web UI/API |
| InfiniDysk frontend | 3000 | Web UI |
| InfiniDysk backend | 8080 | API/WebDAV |
| AltMount | 8088 | Web UI/API; `/live` readiness endpoint |
| Plex Media Server | 32400 | `/web` |
| Jellyfin | 8096 | Web UI/API |
| Emby | 8096 | Web UI/API |



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

Native InfiniDysk 2 uses its backend listener for the native application UI as well. Read the [InfiniDysk guide](../services/core/infinidysk.md) for the selected generation rather than assuming the generation 1 split applies.

</div>



## Arr applications and library tools

| Service | Default port | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Sonarr | 8989 | TV |
| Radarr | 7878 | Movies |
| Lidarr | 8686 | Music |
| Whisparr | 6969 | Adult media |
| Prowlarr | 9696 | Indexers |
| NeutArr | 9705 | Search automation |
| Profilarr | 6868 | Profiles and custom formats |
| Seerr | 5055 | Requests |
| Bazarr | 6767 | Subtitles |
| Tautulli | 8181 | Plex monitoring |
| Pulsarr | 3003 | Watchlist automation |
| Maintainerr | 6246 | Library rules |
| Zilean | 8182 | Lookup API |

These defaults refer to the first configured instance. A second Sonarr or Radarr often receives `8990` or `7879`, but those values are not reserved for a particular instance. See [multi-instance configuration](instances.md).

## Optional access and streaming services

| Service | Default port | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| AIOStreams | 3006 | `/stremio/configure`; addon clients need a stable trusted HTTPS `base_url` |
| mediastorm | 7777 | `/admin` |
| <span class="docs-channel-badge" data-channel="dev" title="Added after the released DUMB 2.23.0 documentation snapshot">Dev</span> Audiobookshelf | 13378 | `/audiobookshelf/`; reverse proxies must support WebSockets |
| Traefik Proxy Admin | 3004 | Web UI/API |
| Authelia | 9091 | Identity portal/API |
| Cloudflared | None | Outbound tunnel connector; no local web UI listener |

Use the [AIOStreams publishing guide](../services/optional/aiostreams.md#publish-aiostreams-for-stremio) for its public addon address. The embedded `/ui/aiostreams` address is not its public `base_url`.

## Storage and database services

| Service | Default port | Protocol |
|---|---:|---|
| Zurg | 9090 | HTTP/WebDAV |
| Phalanx DB | 8888 | HTTP API |
| PostgreSQL | 5432 | PostgreSQL, not HTTP |
| pgAdmin | 5050 | Web UI |

A second Zurg instance often receives `9091`, which also overlaps Authelia's default. Use the assigned port, not an assumed sequence.

## Port collisions

DUMB checks enabled-service ports and can move a conflicting listener to the next available port, then save the result. This includes InfiniDysk frontend/backend ports. Traefik reserves its entry point and dashboard together.

Common default overlaps are:

- Riven and InfiniDysk: `3000` and `8080`.
- Jellyfin and Emby: `8096`.
- A second Zurg instance and Authelia: `9091`.

Docker mappings do not update themselves when an internal listener changes. If a service moves from `8096` to `8097`, update its mapping and any direct consumers. Embedded routing uses DUMB's generated service configuration.

## Publish only the listeners you use

For example, a stack with direct Plex access can publish:

```yaml
ports:
  - "3005:3005"   # DUMB dashboard, API gateway, embedded UIs
  - "32400:32400" # Plex clients
```

Add a service mapping when another application or device needs it. A web UI being available through the dashboard does not expose its native protocol to external clients.

The backend's default `127.0.0.1:8000` listener cannot be exposed by adding `8000:8000` alone. Direct backend access also requires changing `dumb.api_service.host`. Prefer the existing gateway and follow [networking guidance](../deployment/networking.md) when changing exposure.

DUMB authentication protects its own API and dashboard flows. Direct upstream application ports and published Traefik routes need their own access controls. Docker's published-port firewall behavior also depends on the host; see [Docker packet filtering](https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/packet-filtering-firewalls/).

# AltMount (Core Service)

**AltMount** connects your Usenet accounts to Sonarr, Radarr and your media server. Its web interface handles provider accounts, queues, content access and the way completed items enter your library.

In DUMB, AltMount is a core Usenet workflow service. DUMB installs and starts AltMount, supplies its baseline configuration, embeds its UI, and connects enabled Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, and Whisparr instances whose `core_service` includes `altmount`.

---

## First-start checklist

1. Select **AltMount** and your intended Arr applications during DUMB onboarding, then choose the mount mode. Reopen onboarding from **Settings → Launch Onboarding** if needed.
2. Open the AltMount service card. On **DUMB Config**, use **Start** if stopped, then select **Embedded UI**. Create the first administrator in AltMount or sign in to the existing account.
3. Replace first-run WebDAV credentials before exposing the endpoint outside a trusted network. Update dependent clients and restart the affected mount when needed.
4. Add and test at least one TLS-enabled Usenet provider account. Review the selected mount type and path in AltMount's Mount settings; shared accounts must stay within their total connection allowance.
5. Open **AltMount → Configuration → Import**. Choose `NONE`, `SYMLINK` or `STRM` and prepare any required import directory. This choice is separate from the mount mode. Follow [Import strategy and library paths](#import-strategy-and-library-paths) before sending a real item.
6. In each Arr's **Embedded UI**, test the `altmount` entry under **Settings → Download Clients**, then test its indexers. Review **Settings → Media Management → Root Folders** and add that same library folder to your media server.
7. Send one small intended NZB. Follow the queue through import, scan the media library and play it. A successful provider test alone does not check library visibility or playback.



<div class="docs-dev-section" markdown="1">

<p class="docs-dev-section-label">Development update · not in the released 2.23.0 docs</p>

## Setup checklist and remaining work

Choose the mount/import arrangement deliberately. The checklist collects or references provider accounts and guides selected Arr connections. Authorize the AltMount administrator, choose direct/symlink/STRM behavior, provide external mounts and validate paths. Sharing an account does not create an unlimited connection budget.

On recognized guarded versions, enter an administrator name and password and explicitly choose **Create the first AltMount administrator**. DUMB registers only while the native server confirms zero users and open first-user registration, then verifies the authenticated session. Existing administrators are reused rather than recreated. You can also complete this step in AltMount's own UI. The checklist exchanges an authorized temporary administrator login for a protected settings session and removes the submitted password after successful authorization.

The download-client/SABnzbd API key does not authorize administrator settings changes. A settings session can expire; authorize the relevant task again when AltMount rejects it. Administrator authorization does not move library files or enable existing scan/sync schedules.

The WebDAV task reuses authenticated existing custom credentials when possible. To set or rotate them, enter the replacement credentials, review the masked field preview and explicitly approve that exact proposal. DUMB verifies authenticated WebDAV access and keeps the handoff to selected consumers private. Coordinate external clients separately: DUMB cannot rewrite unknown consumers. For an internal rclone mount, changing credentials requires an explicitly authorized AltMount-only restart, which can interrupt active playback. External/no-mount layouts can use the supported native hot configuration path. API/configuration checks do not prove FUSE mounts or the complete playback workflow.

Requires the backend setup-arrangement capability. See [Setup checklist and automation](../../features/setup-checklist.md) for retained tasks, coverage and safe retries.

</div>
